leftEvidence.title: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: After six days Jesus takes three disciples up a high mountain; his face shines, his clothes become white, and Moses and Elijah appear speaking with him.
points.right: Peter denies following crafted myths and says the apostles were eyewitnesses of Jesus’ majesty.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Peter proposes three tents; a bright cloud overshadows them, the voice names the beloved Son and commands listening, and the frightened disciples finally see Jesus alone.
points.right: He recalls honor and glory from God the Father, the beloved-Son declaration, the heard voice, and prophetic Scripture.

payload.posture: Matthew narrates the event; 2 Peter explicitly claims remembered sight and hearing on the holy mountain.

rightEvidence.title: Peter remembers the majestic voice on the holy mountain

payload.tension: The later memory selects majesty, honor, glory, voice, and prophetic confirmation rather than retelling every detail.
payload.title: The mountain scene and Peter’s eyewitness claim
